Which performance results have evidence?

Check the record type and conditions before using a number in a hardware decision.

0approved measured PC records

No permitted measured PC dataset currently supports the selectable exact hardware and game setups. This is an evidence gap, not proof that your PC performs poorly. No measured 1% low, calibrated error or upgrade percentage is supplied.

The console register contains 45 exact game/console contexts and 29 source records. Some contexts remain unverified; sourced mode targets or caps are not the same as sustained measured FPS.

Four different result types

Measured benchmarks
A captured game result with exact hardware, settings, method and permitted provenance. None are approved in the current PC dataset.
Third-party reports
A named original publisher’s observation, linked with its conditions and limitations. It is not testing performed by this site.
Mode targets and caps
A documented output mode or intended frame-rate limit. It does not establish sustained performance in every scene or on a different patch.
Legacy calculations
Unvalidated assumed workloads and synthetic-score arithmetic. These are opt-in demonstrations with no measured calibration or statistical confidence.

Compare like with like

Keep game version, CPU, exact GPU, RAM, driver, resolution, quality, ray tracing, upscaling, frame generation and test scene with every measurement. A synthetic score does not become measured game FPS, and generated frames do not prove an equivalent input-latency improvement.

The register retains its original source inspection dates. Rebuilding this coverage view does not re-verify a game patch. Use the original source and exact console edition before interpreting a target.
